Retail Manager – Domino’s Pizza Sutherland
Business: Domino’s Pizza Sutherland
Address: 55B Eton Street, Sutherland NSW 2232
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing
Salary: AUD $75,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation
About the Business
Domino’s Pizza Sutherland operates as a fast-paced, customer-focused quick service restaurant within the Domino’s Australia network. The store provides high-volume takeaway, delivery, and in-store customer services while maintaining compliance with Domino’s national operational systems, food safety standards, and franchise requirements. The business is committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences through operational excellence, efficient service delivery, strong team leadership, and consistent adherence to Domino’s brand standards.
Serving the Sutherland Shire community and surrounding areas, Domino’s Pizza Sutherland operates in a dynamic and high-volume environment that requires effective operational management, workforce coordination, inventory control, and customer service leadership to ensure ongoing business success.
 
Position Overview
The Retail Manager is responsible for the end-to-end management of Domino’s Pizza Sutherland's daily operations, ensuring efficient store performance, strong financial outcomes, exceptional customer service, and effective team leadership. The role requires hands-on operational involvement within a fast-paced quick service restaurant environment and accountability for workforce management, compliance, inventory control, and operational excellence in accordance with Domino’s Australia policies and procedures.
This is a senior operational role suited to an experienced retail or hospitality professional who thrives in a structured, performance-driven environment and possesses strong leadership and organisational capabilities.
 
Key Responsibilities
Store Operations & Performance
•	Plan, coordinate, and manage daily store operations to achieve sales, productivity, and customer service targets.
•	Ensure compliance with Domino's operational procedures, food safety requirements, workplace health and safety obligations, and franchise standards.
•	Monitor key operational performance indicators including labour costs, food costs, wastage levels, sales performance, and profitability.
•	Coordinate workflow during peak trading periods to maintain service efficiency and customer satisfaction.
•	Identify opportunities to improve operational processes and service delivery standards.
People Leadership & Team Management
•	Recruit, train, roster, supervise, and motivate store employees including shift supervisors, pizza makers, customer service staff, and delivery drivers.
•	Provide ongoing coaching, performance management, and skills development consistent with Domino's training systems and operational expectations.
•	Foster a positive and collaborative workplace culture that promotes accountability, teamwork, and operational excellence.
•	Monitor employee performance and ensure adequate staffing levels are maintained throughout trading hours.
•	Promote compliance with workplace policies and ensure adherence to employment obligations.
Customer Experience & Brand Standards
•	Oversee customer service delivery across takeaway, delivery, and in-store service channels.
•	Resolve customer complaints and service issues promptly and professionally to maintain customer satisfaction and brand reputation.
•	Maintain high standards of store presentation, cleanliness, and food quality at all times.
•	Ensure all products are prepared and delivered in accordance with Domino's quality and service standards.
•	Support the implementation of customer service initiatives aimed at enhancing the overall customer experience.
Stock Management & Cost Control
•	Manage inventory levels, supplier orders, stock deliveries, and stock rotation procedures.
•	Conduct regular stocktakes and monitor food cost variances, wastage levels, and inventory usage.
•	Implement effective cost control measures to support profitability objectives.
•	Ensure store equipment, POS systems, and operational assets are maintained and functioning efficiently.
•	Coordinate with suppliers and internal support teams regarding operational requirements when necessary.
Compliance & Administration
•	Ensure compliance with Fair Work obligations, food safety legislation, workplace health and safety requirements, and Domino's internal compliance policies.
•	Prepare operational reports, sales summaries, labour reports, and performance documentation as required.
•	Maintain accurate records relating to staffing, inventory management, and operational performance.
•	Implement and monitor company policies, procedures, and operational guidelines across all aspects of store management.
•	Support ongoing compliance audits and operational assessments where required.
 
Skills & Experience
Essential Requirements
•	Proven experience in retail or hospitality management within a fast-paced operational environment.
•	Demonstrated leadership capability with experience managing teams, employee rostering, and operational workflows.
•	Strong understanding of inventory management, cost control principles, and retail performance management.
•	Excellent organisational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•	Ability to work effectively under pressure while maintaining high service standards.
•	Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and public holidays as required by operational needs.
•	Preference will be given to suitably qualified Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents.
Preferred Qualifications
•	AQF associate degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma (ANZSCO Skill Level 2); or
•	At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications listed above. In some instances, relevant experience and/or on-the-job training may be required in addition to formal qualifications.
•	Current Food Safety Certification or willingness to obtain.
•	Previous experience within quick service restaurant (QSR), franchised food retail, or hospitality operations will be highly regarded.
•	Experience using point-of-sale systems, workforce management tools, and inventory management systems is desirable.
Work Environment
The Retail Manager role is highly operational and requires active participation on the shop floor alongside store employees. The position demands excellent time management skills, resilience under pressure, strong leadership capabilities, and the ability to manage multiple operational priorities simultaneously within a high-volume service environment. The successful candidate will be expected to lead by example, maintain operational excellence, and contribute positively to the ongoing success of Domino's Pizza Sutherland.

Are you an experienced Mental Health Registered Nurse with a passion for education, leadership, and developing others? Join Central Coast Local Health District (CCLHD) as a Clinical Nurse Educator and play a pivotal role in supporting and empowering our mental health nursing workforce.

About the Opportunity

In this rewarding position, you will help build capability across our acute mental health in-patient services by delivering high-quality clinical education, mentoring staff, and promoting evidence-based practice.

As the Clinical Nurse Educator, you will provide clinical education and training that enhances the knowledge, skills, and confidence of nursing staff within the Mental Health Division. In this role you will:

Deliver engaging clinical education and training to build capability across Mental Health In-Patient Services.

Mentor and support nursing staff to promote evidence-based practice and professional development.

Design, implement, and evaluate education programs that strengthen clinical skills and patient care.

Collaborate with clinical leaders and multidisciplinary teams to identify learning needs and drive continuous improvement.

For more information about this role, please view the Position Description 

About You

We are looking for someone who has:

Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse, with relevant postgraduate clinical or education qualifications (or equivalent experience).

Extensive recent experience in a mental health clinical setting, with a strong commitment to high-quality patient care.

Demonstrated expertise in delivering education, applying adult learning principles, and supporting workforce development.

Excellent communication, collaboration, and leadership skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Confidence using technology to support contemporary clinical education and a commitment to CCLHD's strategic plan and annual priorities of; 'Trusted care. Better health for everyone.'

Applicants must have current work rights in Australia or be a permanent resident or citizen. Unfortunately, we cannot consider applicants who do not meet this requirement.

Benefits

Work-Life Balance: Enjoy an accrued day off each month, 17.5% annual leave loading, and paid parental leave.

Financial Benefits: Boost your take-home pay with salary packaging, save on car costs with novated leasing, and access relocation assistance.

Health & Wellbeing: Stay active with discounted gym memberships (Fitness Passport), free flu vaccinations, telehealth support, and confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) counselling for you and your family. Plus, access discounted private health insurance.

Career Growth: Advance your career with free professional development courses and secondment opportunities.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









About the Role 






Monash Biochemistry Laboratory is seeking enthusiastic and motivated Medical Laboratory Scientists to join our dynamic and highly skilled team. Multiple positions are available, with consideration given to both full-time and part-time appointments.






As a 24-7 diagnostic laboratory, we provide routine and acute biochemistry testing services that support patient care across a diverse clinical setting. Successful applicants will have the opportunity to work with a broad range of analytical platforms and specialised testing services in a fast-paced and collaborative environment. The successful applicant will contribute to the delivery of high-quality diagnostic testing, including: 









Routine and urgent biochemistry testing 












Quality assurance and quality control activities 












Instrument maintenance and troubleshooting 












Result validation and interpretation 












Participation in a rotating roster, including evenings, nights, weekends and public holidays as required 












Specialised testing, including protein electrophoresis and mass spectrometry (where applicable) 















Essential Criteria:









Bachelor of Science (Medical Laboratory Science) or equivalent qualification recognised by AIMS or the AACB. 












Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fast-paced laboratory environment. 












Ability to maintain accuracy and attention to detail while working under pressure. 












Strong organisational, communication and teamwork skills. 












Commitment to providing a high-quality diagnostic service. 















Desirable Criteria:









Previous experience working in a diagnostic Biochemistry laboratory. 












Experience performing and interpreting serum and urine protein electrophoresis. 












Experience in mass spectrometry, including method development, validation and troubleshooting. 












Experience working within a NATA-accredited laboratory environment. 












Familiarity with laboratory information systems and automated chemistry analysers.







For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Kevin Jessen, on (03) 9594 2055. 


Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

We are looking for a special kind of person - a St Vincent's kind of person. Someone who puts compassion, connection and caring for other people at the heart of everything they do.

As a Care Services Employee, you'll be part of an experienced, engaged and dedicated team helping to create a welcoming, professional and supportive care experience for the residents of St Vincent's Care Services, Heathcote.

St Vincent's Care Services Heathcote (locally known as John Paul Village) is a 213 bed facility located 35km from Sydney's CBD. It is situated next to the Royal National Park, one of Sydney's real treasures!

What's on your resume is important, but what's in your heart matters more.
Because at St Vincent's, kindness works for us.

This is a part-time permanent opportunity with PM and Night shifts available.

Things that work for us:

Certificate III in Individual Support-Aged Care or similar qualifications essential.

6 months+ experience in a similar role with residential aged care experience highly regarded.

Availability to work PM and night shifts throughout the week.

Excellent customer service and communication skills.

Experience with AutumnCare (or similar software) with ability to maintain excellent records.

Understanding of Aged Care, resident rights-responsibilities with ability to follow the care plan.

Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check and NDIS Worker Screening Check will be a requirement of this role.

Things that work for you:

Competitive salary packaging options up to $15,990, Novated leasing, plus an optional Meals and Entertainment card up to $2,650 per annum

Opportunity to work for the nation's largest Catholic not-for-profit health and aged care provider, with a rapidly growing and progressive vision

Friendly team environment with a great community care spirit

Ability to visibly see your impact on the business and its service

No cost uniforms and training

Free annual flu vaccination

Employee Assistance Program for staff and their families

Access to the Fitness Passport (FP)

Why become part of the St Vincent's Care family?

Because you're like us, you believe that every act of kindness makes the world a better place. Better for everyone who lives in the 20+ facilities and locations we operate in Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria. Better for all our staff and employees, who work tirelessly to provide the highest levels of care and quality of life for our clients. And better support for the local communities we play an important role in and continue to support.

For more than 175 years, St Vincent's Care Services (SVCS) has been a leading Catholic provider of Aged Care Services in Australia, and the legacy of compassion, justice, integrity and excellence entrusted to us by the Sisters of Charity and their Founder Mary Aitkenhead continues to inspire our work today.

Our spiritual and hospital-based heritage has taught us that wellness is about more than medical needs. It's about building a true partnership around trust and respect. That's why we take a person-centred approach - delivering holistic, individual care that achieves wellbeing for mind, body and spirit.

At St Vincent's we value inclusivity and diversity and acknowledge the important of creating a work environment that is welcome, safe, fair and impartial and invite people from all backgrounds to join our caring family.

Reconciliation Action Plan
St Vincent's Health Australia embraces Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people's unique perspectives, knowledge, and cultural. We strive to achieve better physical, mental, and spiritual health outcomes through continued connection with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. We understand the need to effectively engage with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities to influence decision making at all levels and to create opportunity through sustainable and culturally safe employment.

As part of our Commitment to Reconciliation and Closing the Gap in employment related outcomes, we encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. For further information, visit http:--www.svha.org.au-about-us-reconciliation or get in contact at indigenouscareers@svha.org.au

Interested? Apply online!

No agencies please.

Closing Date:
9 August 2026 11:59pm

At St Vincent's we acknowledge the importance of creating a work environment that is welcoming, safe, equitable and inclusive for Aboriginal and-or Torres Strait Islander Employees. As part of our Commitment to Reconciliation and Closing the Gap in employment related outcomes, we encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.
